Subject: Long-context evals — initial findings

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick summary from our side and a few asks so we can decide next steps.

What we tried: we ran a quick pass over a 180k-token transcript corpus (customer interviews + product docs) and tried two open checkpoints we had on-prem. Observations:
- Truncation: models are consistently dropping content beyond ~65k tokens (exact spot varies by run). This leads to missing context in downstream summarization.
- Summarization fidelity: when prompts ask for extractive highlights, recall drops quickly beyond the 50k mark; hallucinations increase when context is truncated mid-paragraph.
- Latency: we saw token generation slowdowns once context exceeded ~40k tokens (likely KV cache thrash).

Attached: small sample of failing cases and the prompt set we used. High-level asks:
1) Can Redwood recommend model variants and runtime settings we should try (quantization, chunking, caching)?
2) Do you have benchmark links showing long-context behavior and truncation thresholds for your recommended models?
3) What's a realistic pilot plan (time + cost) to validate on our workload?

Thanks — we can share more logs if helpful.

-John
Director of Applied AI
Acme Corp

Attachments: acme_long_context_eval_results_v1.pdf, prompt_set_acme_v2.jsonl, sample_docs_acme.zip

John — thanks for the clear notes and the attachments. Appreciate the sample docs, that made it much easier to reproduce quickly. High-level answers up front and a proposed next step below.

Short answers / recommendations:
- Models: start with Redwood-Open-Llama-70B (fp16) for baseline and RW-Instruct-65B-q4_0 for a cost-optimized run. We also recommend trying a 13B instruction-tuned variant for a control if you need lower latency.
- Runtime settings: enable persistent KV cache between related calls, use a chunked input strategy (sliding window with 8k overlaps) rather than single huge context, and evaluate q4_0 quantization profile if you want a cost/throughput tradeoff.
- Benchmarks: I uploaded a short benchmark summary and run scripts to the shared Drive (link below). We have internal perf graphs for long-context windows up to 200k tokens for the 70B family (look at the "kv-cache-threshold" section).

Proposed pilot (recommended):
- Scope: 3 representative workflows (interview summarization, long-form doc QA, multi-doc summarization) using your sample corpus.
- Setup: Redwood Dedicated reserved pool (2x A100-equivalent) for isolated runs + shared hosted for comparison. Dev will help set the exact infra config.
- Duration: 2 weeks for exploratory runs + 1 week for analysis and a recap.
- Outputs: per-workflow precision/recall at 25k/50k/100k/150k windows, latency and cost per 1k tokens, specific failure cases and recommended mitigations.

Next steps: Dev, can you take point on an infra config and an estimated cost? Michael, can you add the benchmark artifact and a suggested prompt set tweak? John/Sara, would next Tue 10am PT work to review the pilot plan?

Subject: Re: Long-context evals — runtime/config suggestions

Following up with concrete runtime notes from infra/SE perspective. Quick wins (low lift) vs. deeper changes:

Quick wins:
- Use continuous KV cache for related conversational threads; this avoids re-encoding repeated prefixes and reduces effective token processing.
- Chunking: break large documents into ~32k token chunks with an 8k overlap and feed as progressive context. For summarization tasks, run an item-level extractive pass first and then synthesize summaries across chunks.
- Model choice: Redwood-Open-Llama-70B (fp16) for quality; RW-Instruct-65B-q4_0 for cost tests. The 13B control helps isolate latency vs. quality tradeoffs.

Deeper changes (recommended for a follow-on test):
- Sliding-window summarization: run an intermediate summarizer that produces 2–3 paragraph summaries per chunk, then feed those into a final summarization step. This reduces end-to-end hallucinations vs. single-pass summarization on truncated context.
- KV cache tuning: increase per-worker KV cache size and pin hot layers when possible; this reduces cache eviction thrash for >50k contexts.
- Quantization note: q4_0 gives good throughput with minimal quality drop for emergent summarization tasks, but we should validate on your prompt-set (attached).

Estimated pilot infra & cost (very rough):
- Dedicated: 2x A100-equivalent for 3 weeks (including setup/test) — estimate $28k–$40k depending on utilization and burst days.
- Hosted: cheaper but expect higher variability and lower deterministic throughput; useful as a comparison.

I've attached a sample run script (internal) and will share a small perf artifact in the Drive folder. Dev can run an initial 1-day micro-run if you can confirm a small subset of 10 representative docs.

- Dev

Attachments referenced: sample_run.sh (in Drive), prompt_set_acme_v2.jsonl
